newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt proposes talks on lower highway tolls.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt proposes talks on lower highway tolls.

text.p: The Hungarian government has authorised the Ministry of Transport to start talks on reducing controversial tolls on motorways operated by new concessionary companies.
"The government and the concessionaries have to share the risks involved in the reduction of tolls," government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.
Tolls were first introduced in Hungary last March.

The 850 forints ($4.85) fee for a 56 km stretch of the motorway south from Budapest has provoked protests from Hungarian motorists while mayors of villages on the road parallel to the highway complained of increased traffic.
The government is looking for a "sizeable reduction of the tolls" Kiss said, adding that he could not give any figures before the negotiations were completed.

The government's proposal is that it and the concession companies should bear part of the losses due to a traffic reduction from current levels and share the profit if the lower toll results in higher turnover.
According to M5 operator Alfoldi Koncesszios Autopalya figures, since the toll was introduced last December, the daily traffic halved to an average of 7,000 cars a day.
A Budapest court ruled last year that the country' first toll of 1,000 forints for a 43 km stretch of the M1 Budapest-Vienna highway was excessively high and should be reduced to 550 forints.

Following the court's decision, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and other banks suspended last December for three months the financing of further projects on both the M1 and M5.
